English translation

Marta Fogagnolo

Here lies Eutychianos, having lived in Christ. He died eight days before the Kalends of August, during the consulship of Anicius Auchenius Bassus and Flavius Philippus.

commentary

The epitaph opens at l. 1 with the standard formula ἐνθάδε κεῖται, followed by the name of the deceased, Eutychianos (for the name in Sicily, see CIL X 7006 = ISic000005; LGPN IIIA, 178). The expression ζήσας ἐν | Χ(ριστ)ῷ (ll. 2–3) is also attested in other Christian epitaphs (cf. I.Pal.Tertia Ia 258, ll. 3–4) and serves to emphasize the deceased's principal virtue, namely that of being a believer (Agnello 1953, 99). At ll. 3–5, the date of death is introduced by the verb τελευτᾷ and is further specified by the consular dating, during the consulship of Anicius Auchenius Bassus and Flavius Philippus, corresponding to AD 408. Below the text was a symbol that has been interpreted either as an ivy leaf or as an inverted D, representing the Latin abbreviation depositus (Manni Piraino 1973, 31).
